- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid overshoot.
- If recent history shows sharp upward moves followed by a drop, model tends to overcorrect — dampen forecast peak and allow gradual decline.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid false optimism.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in early days of forecast horizon, assume momentum bias — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for next period.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive but true outcome is consistently below forecast, reduce forecast by 3–5% to reflect mean reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, if first 3–5 days show large divergence, assume lagged sentiment effect — adjust forecast to align with sentiment trend from last 7–10 days.
- If sentiment spikes after a low, model often overreacts — reduce forecast peak and add a slight downward bias for next 3–5 days.
